steps.label: The names
steps.margin_note: Both names and the year. Two lines.
lines: was proposed by SUTTON and BOVERI, in 1902.
steps.why: Two workers reached the same conclusion independently, which is why both names are always given together.
common_mistakes: Naming Mendel. Mendel knew nothing of chromosomes.
Naming Morgan. Morgan proved the theory later with Drosophila; Sutton and Boveri proposed it.
steps.memory_tip: Sutton and Boveri proposed it; Morgan proved it.

steps.label: What the theory says
steps.margin_note: State the link and the parallel behaviour. This half is often left out.

lines.text: Mendel's factors are carried on chromosomes

lines: The theory states that Mendel's FACTORS (genes)
The behaviour of chromosomes during meiosis
exactly parallels the behaviour of Mendel's
factors: both occur in pairs and both segregate.
steps.why: Chromosomes pair and separate at meiosis exactly as Mendel said his factors must, and that parallel is the entire argument of the theory.
common_mistakes: Saying the theory discovered chromosomes. Chromosomes were already known; the theory linked them to Mendel's factors.
Giving only the names. The second mark is for the content.
steps.memory_tip: Chromosomes behave the way Mendel's factors had to behave.
